name: Selpercatinib for RET-Mutant Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma
histology: medullary thyroid carcinoma (calcitonin-producing parafollicular C-cell carcinoma)

biomarkers.RET: pathogenic variant present (germline or somatic RET mutation)
biomarkers.note: This regimen is biomarker-gated to a RET pathogenic variant (germline RET in hereditary MTC/MEN2, or somatic RET in sporadic MTC). Selpercatinib is a selective RET inhibitor and is a category 1 preferred option specifically for RET-mutant disease; RET-independent multikinase inhibitors (cabozantinib, vandetanib) are the category 1 options when RET status does not direct a selective inhibitor. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026, Medullary Carcinoma (MEDU).

lineOfTherapy: preferred category 1 systemic option for symptomatic or progressive RET-mutant advanced, metastatic, or recurrent/persistent medullary thyroid carcinoma (first-line per LIBRETTO-531)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: RET pathogenic variant (germline or somatic) confirmed
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy, Medullary Carcinoma (MEDU-4): Positive for RET PV, Selpercatinib (category 1), line 3122 to 3123

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: symptomatic or progressing advanced, metastatic, or recurrent/persistent medullary thyroid carcinoma
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Discussion Medullary Carcinoma (LIBRETTO-531, first-line selpercatinib vs cabozantinib/vandetanib), line 5516 and line 5559 to 5562

drugs.name: Selpercatinib

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 70618 (selpercatinib, LIBRETTO-001: 'The recommended dose is 160 mg twice per day')

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 70618. Selpercatinib 160 mg PO TWICE DAILY (represented here as continuous daily dosing; twice-daily frequency is source-stated) for patients at or above 50 kg. DeVita line 70618 states selpercatinib's uniform registered recommended dose (160 mg twice per day) in the NSCLC RET chapter; this is the drug's single, tumor-type-agnostic registered dose, not an MTC-specific citation. The medullary thyroid indication and the same 160 mg twice-daily dose are grounded for MTC by Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026: Medullary Carcinoma selpercatinib category 1 for RET PV positive (MEDU-4, thyroid.txt line 3123) and the phase 3 LIBRETTO-531 first-line RET-mutant MTC trial (thyroid.txt line 3288 reference; Discussion line 5515 to 5517). The 160 mg twice-daily dose is clinically correct for RET-mutant MTC and is retained (not VERIFY). Given continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

regimen.cycles: continuous until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; not a fixed cycle count
supportiveCare: blood-pressure control: hypertension is common with selpercatinib; monitor and treat.
monitor for hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST), QT prolongation, hemorrhage, and hypersensitivity per labeling.
monitor calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) as MTC tumor markers for response.
avoid abrupt discontinuation without taper per labeling if on prolonged therapy.

monitoring: ECG for QT prolongation and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, or hypertension
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for grade 3 to 4 or intolerable toxicity; resume at a reduced dose per labeling once recovered; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 70618 (selpercatinib uniform registered dose 160 mg twice per day, stated in the NSCLC RET chapter; tumor-type-agnostic registered dose); RET as an actionable driver in medullary thyroid carcinoma

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, Medullary Carcinoma (MEDU-4): Selpercatinib category 1 for RET PV positive, cabozantinib and vandetanib category 1 (line 3122 to 3123); Discussion Medullary Carcinoma (LIBRETTO-531 first-line selpercatinib vs cabozantinib/vandetanib; selpercatinib and pralsetinib preferred for RET-mutant disease), line 5515 to 5517 and 5559 to 5562; LIBRETTO-531 primary reference Hadoux et al. NEJM 2023 (line 3288)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for selpercatinib in RET-mutant medullary thyroid carcinoma (StewardMD reference disease medullary_thyroid_carcinoma). The regimen is biomarker-gated to a RET pathogenic variant (germline or somatic). The MTC indication and category 1 preferred status are grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026, Medullary Carcinoma (MEDU-4, line 3122 to 3123) and the LIBRETTO-531 first-line data (Discussion, line 5516, line 5559 to 5562). The selpercatinib dose (160 mg twice daily) is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. line 70618, which states the drug's uniform registered recommended dose in the NSCLC RET chapter; this is selpercatinib's single, tumor-type-agnostic registered dose. The MTC indication and the same 160 mg twice-daily dose are grounded for medullary thyroid carcinoma by Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026 (Medullary Carcinoma selpercatinib category 1, MEDU-4 thyroid.txt line 3123) and the phase 3 LIBRETTO-531 first-line RET-mutant MTC trial (thyroid.txt line 3288; Discussion line 5515 to 5517). The dose is clinically correct for RET-mutant MTC and is retained (not VERIFY). The alternative first-line category 1 agents cabozantinib and vandetanib are RET-independent multikinase inhibitors; the frequently cited cabozantinib 140 mg once-daily MTC dose is NOT printed in the provided thyroid, DeVita, or Harrison sources and would require VERIFY if cabozantinib were substituted. ISMP tall-man not applicable to these agent names. No field is set to VERIFY in this selpercatinib model. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
